findings.description: Long-lived AWS access keys are embedded in EC2 user data. User data is stored in Terraform state and is retrievable from the instance metadata service by processes on the instance, exposing credentials that may grant an attacker AWS API access.

The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, so encryption relies on an account-level default that is not established in this configuration. Data written to this volume may therefore be stored unencrypted.
This snapshot is created from aws_ebs_volume.web_host_storage, which is not configured for encryption. The snapshot can consequently retain the volume's data without encryption at rest.
TCP/22 is permitted from 0.0.0.0/0. The associated web_host instance is launched in a public-IP subnet with a default route to an internet gateway, making SSH reachable from arbitrary Internet hosts.
All protocols and ports may egress to 0.0.0.0/0. This gives a compromised instance unrestricted external connectivity, weakening network containment.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPv4 addresses to instances launched in this subnet. With its internet-gateway route and the attached web_host security group, this exposes the instance's permitted services to the Internet.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPv4 addresses to instances launched in this subnet, which is associated with a route table that has a default route to an internet gateway. Future workloads in this subnet can become Internet-reachable without an explicit public-address decision.
The bucket receiving VPC Flow Logs has no configured server-side encryption. Sensitive network metadata in the logs may be stored without an explicit encryption-at-rest control.
